key_insight: On coarse-grained turbulence data, only linear constant-coefficient constraints remain valid under filtering, so enforcing the original nonlinear PDE residual can bake in an incorrect closure.
engineering_relevance: For neural operators in fluid mechanics, a cheap Fourier-space projection can enforce physically valid constraints exactly, improving stability and rollout quality with minimal training overhead.
method: Train a Fourier neural operator on coarse turbulence data.
Project each output onto the divergence-free / momentum-conserving constraint set in closed form using FFTs.
For energy balance, learn a constant subgrid flux closure before enforcing the constraint.
evidence_signal: In 2D turbulence, projection reduced continuity error to 5.0×10^-7 and momentum-balance error to 8.6×10^-11, while increasing bounded 448-step rollouts from 0.18 to 0.87; on Kolmogorov flow it was ~3,300× cheaper per trajectory than test-time optimization.
watch_item: The projection only guarantees constraints that survive coarse-graining; nonlinear laws require an explicit closure model before they can be enforced reliably.
paper_title: Only Linear Constraints Survive Coarse-Graining: Evaluating Physics-Constrained Neural Operators on Stochastically Forced Turbulence
